executive_summary:
## Executive Summary

It's launch week for **Hermes Desktop**, and the headline is **Bot Screen**: **NousResearch**'s [new feature lets you live-stream any agent's screen or session in real time, with human take-over built in](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-ef6b4179c4fa). It arrived alongside **Teknium**'s [companion launch of interactive desktop passthrough for **Hermes Agent**](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-4784626f2a61). The announcement was the day's top post (~367k views), supported by [official docs and a **tonbistudio** walkthrough](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-d84a2bc0a85d), and community sentiment was emphatically positive — ["Finallllly!"](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-014ad26a44c6) and ["Much needed!"](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-48968e1c836e) replies frame it as a long-requested feature finally landing.

Beyond the launch, the ecosystem showed healthy grassroots momentum: **rlaope** announced [**oh-my-hermes (OMH)** support for **Jev** skills, plugins, and model routing](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-415aecf318f8), and [open-sourced **jeval** for evaluating and visualizing Jev results](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-8530d32deea5) — positioning OMH as [an all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent users](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-b4d141253a4f). On the maintenance side, **Teknium** triaged publicly and actively: [dismissed a reported cache issue pending a reproducible bug report](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-d5a2f794eeec), [confirmed a quick fix for a user-reported problem](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-3e1742f36c0b), and [corrected attribution of a discussed feature to Nous rather than Anthropic](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-992950038a21) — a visible maintainer presence that reinforced trust during launch week.

On the tips front, **NousResearch** reminded users that [**Hermes** can run over **iMessage** with any model of their choosing](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-768697783517) — another example of ongoing efforts to lower friction and highlight the agent's model-agnostic design. Rounding out the day, community chatter weighed in on **Claude Opus 5.5** (released September 22), with **rlaope** [calling the model "crazy" (impressive) while staying lukewarm on Claude Code](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-797e0ee6c95e) — timely competitor context running alongside the Hermes launch coverage.
executive_summary_html:
Executive Summary

It's launch week for Hermes Desktop, and the headline is Bot Screen: NousResearch's new feature lets you live-stream any agent's screen or session in real time, with human take-over built in. It arrived alongside Teknium's companion launch of interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent. The announcement was the day's top post (~367k views), supported by official docs and a tonbistudio walkthrough, and community sentiment was emphatically positive — "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" replies frame it as a long-requested feature finally landing.

Beyond the launch, the ecosystem showed healthy grassroots momentum: rlaope announced oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev skills, plugins, and model routing, and open-sourced jeval for evaluating and visualizing Jev results — positioning OMH as an all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent users. On the maintenance side, Teknium triaged publicly and actively: dismissed a reported cache issue pending a reproducible bug report, confirmed a quick fix for a user-reported problem, and corrected attribution of a discussed feature to Nous rather than Anthropic — a visible maintainer presence that reinforced trust during launch week.

On the tips front, NousResearch reminded users that Hermes can run over iMessage with any model of their choosing — another example of ongoing efforts to lower friction and highlight the agent's model-agnostic design. Rounding out the day, community chatter weighed in on Claude Opus 5.5 (released September 22), with rlaope calling the model "crazy" (impressive) while staying lukewarm on Claude Code — timely competitor context running alongside the Hermes launch coverage.
